en-US.name: SignalGuard
en-US.subtitle: Internet & cellular monitoring
en-US.description:
SignalGuard helps people on call check that their iPhone remains connected.

INTERNET AND CELLULAR NETWORK, CHECKED SEPARATELY
Choose Internet access, cellular network registration, or both before starting. Working Wi-Fi does not hide lost cellular registration, and switching from Wi-Fi to working mobile data does not itself trigger an Internet alert.

ONE TAP TO START
Start a guard immediately with the large power button. Use the default 24-hour limit or choose an earlier end time. Status is shown in the app and through the iOS continued-processing Live Activity.

ALERTS FOR PERSISTENT INTERRUPTIONS
An enabled condition must remain unconfirmed for about 60 seconds before an alert. Brief interruptions are recorded without an alert. Acknowledge an incident to stop its reminders; full recovery also cancels reminders automatically.

MONITORING INTERRUPTED? RESUME EXPLICITLY
iOS may stop a background monitoring task. SignalGuard keeps a local watchdog notification scheduled to warn when monitoring can no longer be confirmed. Tap that notification or use Resume in the app to attempt to continue until the original end time.

LOCAL HISTORY, NO ACCOUNT
Review guards, interruptions and incidents on your iPhone. No advertising, analytics, tracking, telemetry or cloud history. Internet checks make minimal HTTPS requests to external connectivity-check endpoints without SignalGuard user or device identifiers.

IMPORTANT LIMITS
SignalGuard checks Internet availability and cellular network registration. It cannot guarantee receipt of telephone calls or permanent background execution. Notifications depend on iOS and your settings; this version does not use Critical Alerts. A powered-off phone cannot monitor or notify.

Requires iPhone with iOS 26 or later. English and Spanish, following your app language in iOS. Free to use.
en-US.promotionalText: Check Internet and cellular network independently. Start with one tap, review local history, and get warned if monitoring is interrupted.

es-ES.name: SignalGuard
es-ES.subtitle: Internet y red móvil
es-ES.description:
SignalGuard ayuda a las personas de guardia a comprobar que su iPhone mantiene la conectividad.

INTERNET Y RED MÓVIL, POR SEPARADO
Elige acceso a Internet, registro en la red móvil o ambas condiciones antes de empezar. Una conexión Wi-Fi operativa no oculta la pérdida de registro móvil. Pasar de Wi-Fi a datos móviles que funcionan no provoca por sí solo un aviso de Internet.

ACTIVA CON UN TOQUE
Inicia una guardia al momento con el botón central. Utiliza el límite predeterminado de 24 horas o elige una hora de fin anterior. Consulta el estado en la app y en la actividad en directo de la tarea de iOS.

AVISOS ANTE INTERRUPCIONES PERSISTENTES
Una condición seleccionada debe permanecer sin confirmar unos 60 segundos antes de generar un aviso. Las interrupciones breves quedan registradas sin alertar. Reconoce un incidente para detener sus recordatorios; la recuperación completa también los cancela automáticamente.

SI SE INTERRUMPE LA MONITORIZACIÓN
iOS puede detener la tarea en segundo plano. SignalGuard mantiene programado un aviso local de vigilancia para advertir cuando ya no puede confirmar la monitorización. Toca ese aviso o pulsa Reanudar en la app para intentar continuar hasta la hora de fin original.

HISTORIAL LOCAL, SIN CUENTA
Revisa guardias, interrupciones e incidentes en tu iPhone. Sin publicidad, analítica, seguimiento, telemetría ni historial en la nube. Las comprobaciones de Internet realizan solicitudes HTTPS mínimas a puntos de comprobación externos sin identificadores de usuarios ni de dispositivos de SignalGuard.

LÍMITES IMPORTANTES
SignalGuard comprueba el acceso a Internet y el registro en la red móvil. No garantiza la recepción de llamadas ni una ejecución permanente en segundo plano. Los avisos dependen de iOS y de tus ajustes; esta versión no utiliza avisos críticos. Un teléfono apagado no puede monitorizar ni avisar.

Para iPhone con iOS 26 o posterior. Inglés y español, según el idioma de la app en iOS. Uso gratuito.
es-ES.promotionalText: Comprueba Internet y red móvil por separado. Activa con un toque, consulta el historial local y recibe un aviso si se interrumpe la monitorización.

reviewNotes:
SignalGuard is a free iPhone-only connectivity monitoring utility, requiring iOS 26+. No login, demo credentials, purchases or remote backend.

Use a physical iPhone with an active cellular service and working Internet. On Home choose Internet, cellular network, or both (at least one required). Allow local notifications with alerts, sound and Time Sensitive delivery. Preflight checks run automatically; an unconfirmed selected prerequisite blocks Start. Tap the central power button to start. Default guard limit is 24 hours; Choose end time can shorten it. Tap the same button to stop; no confirmation dialog. Home never reports active until native startup is confirmed.

Native implementation: public BGContinuedProcessingTask with immediate/fail submission; registration at launch; real duration progress and the system's own Live Activity. Swift owns monitoring, independent of JavaScript/background timers. No audio/location/VoIP background modes or private APIs. NWPathMonitor plus bounded minimal HTTPS checks to Google generate_204 / Microsoft connecttest.txt confirms Internet; CoreTelephony serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology reports registration, not call deliverability or signal strength.

Allow an enabled condition to remain unavailable for 60 seconds to exercise local Time Sensitive alerts. Acknowledge stops that incident's reminders; full recovery cancels them. There is no Critical Alerts entitlement. A separate 90-second local watchdog is refreshed by native heartbeats. iOS may terminate execution; the pre-scheduled watchdog attempts to warn. Tap the interruption notification or Resume in the app for an explicit new immediate task, retaining the original end/conditions. Opening via the icon never silently restarts.

History is device-local and links interrupted/resumed segments without counting gaps as monitoring. Privacy/support are accessible via the information button on History. No analytics/telemetry or user/device identifiers in probes. Production excludes diagnostics and sample history. No guaranteed call reception or permanent execution claim.

CoreTelephony and background runtime must be reviewed on a physical iPhone; simulator/Expo Go cannot provide this native safety functionality.
